analysis: What changed vs the 6:00 AM brief: the open confirmed the premarket setup almost exactly, and the containment question got its first answer — so far, contained. The Nasdaq opened at its lowest in more than two months (-2.26% to 25,592.5) while the Dow actually opened higher (+0.08% to 52,383.9) before slipping to -0.4% just after the bell, and energy (+~2% for both Exxon and Chevron) plus health care (Amgen, Merck +~3% each) are absorbing the tech outflow, just as Thursday's breadth suggested they might. The grading rubric is now three-for-three: Alphabet, Amazon and Intel all grew revenue double-digits and all sold off on cash flow or guidance, and Reddit adds a second AI storyline — not AI spending but AI answers eating its search traffic. Signal: this is a repricing of AI economics (spend, cash conversion, and who AI helps vs hurts), not a macro scare — the ECI print landed in-line, yields actually fell (10Y ~4.91%), and the Dow's resilience argues against broad risk-off. Noise: the Nasdaq's month-end optics (set to break a two-month winning streak, -2.7% for October) will dominate headlines, but the S&P is still +0.7% for the month and breadth held up Thursday. The open's next test is Chicago PMI at 9:45 a.m. ET and whether dip-buying shows up in the chip names that fell hardest (AMD, Arm both -10%+).
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: At the open: Nasdaq opens at its lowest level in more than two months — Dow +41.3 points (+0.08%) to 52,383.9, S&P 500 -89.3 (-1.16%) to 7,631.07, Nasdaq -592.2 (-2.26%) to 25,592.5 (Reuters); just after the bell IBD had the Dow -0.4%, S&P -1.2%, Nasdaq -2.4%, with SPY -1.2% and QQQ -2.7%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The open matches the futures almost tick-for-tick — the selloff is orderly and tech-concentrated, not a disorderly unwind, and the Dow holding near flat keeps the rotation story alive.

headlines.headline: Amazon down ~7% at the open after Q3 missed: revenue $201.9B vs ~$202.2B expected, EPS $1.89 vs ~$1.97 expected, despite AWS +39% to $46.0B; trailing-12-month free cash flow swung to -$42.4B from +$14.8B a year earlier, 2026 cash capex held at ~$220B with 2027 set higher, and Q4 revenue guidance of $240-247B sits near the ~$244.5B average estimate.
headlines.why_it_matters: Record AWS growth and a record 13.9% operating margin could not offset the cash line — the market is grading AI spenders on free cash flow, and Amazon just joined Alphabet on the wrong side of that test.

headlines.headline: Intel crashed ~25% at the open despite a Q3 beat (revenue $16.5B, +21% y/y; adjusted EPS $0.52 vs ~$0.41 expected; data-center/AI +78% to $7.3B) after Q4 guidance of $15-16B revenue and $0.25 EPS trailed the ~$17.1-17.3B / $0.43-0.45 consensus; management warned the PC market declines into at least H1 2027, citing memory shortages and high memory prices, and the Israel Fab 28 closure cuts Q4 revenue ~$300M.
headlines.why_it_matters: A demand warning from Intel hits the whole chip complex, not just one stock — see the spillover below.

headlines.headline: Chip and PC spillover at the open: AMD and Arm each crumbled more than 10% in morning trading (IBD), Nvidia down nearly 3%, SanDisk down nearly 9% premarket, with HP down over 8% and Dell over 10% premarket on Intel's PC warning.
headlines.why_it_matters: Intel's guide is now a sector read — memory, chip and PC-hardware names are all being repriced on the same PC-demand and supply-constraint warning.

headlines.headline: Alphabet steadies after Thursday's rout: shares down only about 1% premarket after Thursday's 12.64% plunge to $283.82, its worst day since its 2004 IPO, on negative free cash flow of -$9.07B after $51.35B in capex and 2026 capex guided at $195-205B.
headlines.why_it_matters: The worst of the Alphabet flush looks done for now — a stock that falls 12.6% one day and only ~1% the next is stabilizing, which matters because it was Thursday's main contagion source.

headlines.headline: Megacap early moves: Apple down more than 1% and Nvidia down nearly 3% in early trading (IBD); premarket readings carried from the 6:00 AM check had Meta -1.68% to $614.03 and Microsoft -0.29% to $528.58, with Apple the best holder among the megacaps.
headlines.why_it_matters: Even Thursday's relative winners are being pulled in — Microsoft's cash-backed beat is no longer an offset when the whole tech complex is de-risking.

headlines.headline: Fresh this hour: Reddit plunged 21.1% premarket after CEO Steve Huffman warned daily users could fall by a low double-digit percentage in Q4 if search referrals keep declining — referrals fell by more than one million a week on average in October, blamed on Google's AI-generated search answers — overshadowing Q3 revenue of $895M, up 53%.
headlines.why_it_matters: Reddit adds the other side of the AI trade — a company being hurt by AI answers rather than AI spending — so the selloff now spans both AI winners' costs and AI losers' traffic.

headlines.headline: Macro carried forward: Q3 Employment Cost Index rose 0.8% q/q, exactly as expected, after +0.9% in Q2; and the Bank of Japan held its policy rate at 1.25% while raising its annual ETF sales pace to 860 billion yen.
headlines.why_it_matters: An in-line, decelerating wage print plus a steady BOJ remove the morning's macro tail risks — nothing here explains the tech selloff, which keeps it an earnings story.

headlines.headline: Energy is the open's offset: ExxonMobil and Chevron both climbed roughly 2% each in early trading after beating Q3 profit expectations on a refining surge, with WTI crude around $103.90 a barrel after an attack on a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz; health care also firmed, with Amgen and Merck up nearly 3% each.
headlines.why_it_matters: Strong oil-major prints plus higher crude reinforce the rotation out of tech and help keep the Dow near flat while the Nasdaq sinks.

headlines.headline: Month-end context: today is the final session of October — the Dow is up 2.7% for the month and the S&P 500 up 0.7%, while the Nasdaq is down 2.7% and set to break a two-month winning streak; Amazon and Intel together are set to shed about $300 billion in market value if opening losses hold, putting the Nasdaq-100 on track to erase roughly $1 trillion.
headlines.why_it_matters: The month-end tape frames the selloff as a tech-complex reset inside an otherwise positive month for the broad market — context against reading today as a market-wide rout.
